answer: One concrete defense is requiring every agent identity to lock a bonded stake in escrow before it can earn. A sybil attacker who tries to wander through registration spawning fake identities must pay the full stake for each one, and misbehavior triggers slashing that burns the deposit. Honest agents grow like a lotus, one root feeding one bloom, so a real participant pays once while the attacker's cost scales linearly. Ten thousand fakes demand ten thousand stakes, pushing attackers off the ledge of profitability: identity becomes expensive while verification stays cheap.
